title: Future human-reference rare-Soul prevalence guardrail
scope: Reusable project-level default for a future named human-reference population only after explicit adoption by that work's manifest; not automatically binding on any current or future setting, Enuma, another species, or detailed world canon.
approval_evidence: The Author explicitly selected Soul A and instructed that it be recorded with this bounded project-level future-setting scope on 2026-08-12.
question: What provisional rare-Soul prevalence and topology should future human-reference population modelling use before a named setting population is defined?
selection: Offer the exact-decimal provisional prevalence 0.001, approximately 1 in 1,000, as the project default for a future named human-reference population when its work manifest explicitly adopts this decision. A qualifying rare Soul is a heterogeneous typed profile, never one scalar quantity. The prevalence is not Mage prevalence. An independent work may override it only through its own Author decision.
alternatives: Option A: exact-decimal prevalence 0.001 with heterogeneous typed Soul profiles; selected.
Other prevalence values or scalar Soul models; not selected and not authorised by this decision.
rationale: This supplies a bounded modelling prior without pretending a future society, population denominator, Soul threshold, or Mage correlation has already been worldbuilt.
evidence: Author selection Soul A and bounded-scope instruction dated 2026-08-12.
litrpg-system/cal0/canonical/litrpg-system-specification.md: Soul structure is typed and non-scalar.
litrpg-system/cal0/guide/litrpg-system-residual-uncertainty-register.md: rare-Soul prevalence remains a world-level input.
consequences: Future human-reference population models may use the exact-decimal prior 0.001 only after naming and scoping their population.
Rare-Soul membership must be represented through heterogeneous typed Soul dimensions and thresholds, never a universal Soul score.
The prior must not be reported or used as the prevalence of Mages, magical affinity, classes, Skills, talents, social elites, or exceptional people generally.
This decision creates no named people, culture, institution, geography, history, or setting fact.
No work inherits this guardrail silently; its manifest must cite the decision URI and adopted scope.
A work-specific override requires its own explicit Author decision and does not rewrite this project default for other works.
residual_unknowns: The future human-reference population and eligible denominator are not yet named.
The typed qualification threshold and distribution across Soul dimensions remain undefined.
Correlation with magical capability, vocation, culture, ancestry, age, and environment remains undefined.
Other species and populations remain out of scope.
Which future works, if any, will adopt this default remains undefined.
reopening_conditions: A named human-reference population is defined and evidence supports a different prevalence.
The operational typed qualification threshold is defined and changes the implied eligible denominator.
Population modelling exposes a contradiction or unusable outcome.
The Author explicitly reopens the guardrail.
